# @openengine/web

> A WebGPU engine on a web page: import it as an ES module, create an engine on a canvas, load glTF models, orbit a camera, light the scene with a physical sun and sky, and read or write any entity's components. Every object is a handle on an engine entity; every property reads and writes the engine directly.

> Early access (alpha): the API changes between releases. Install with `npm install @openengine/web@alpha`.

Write pages as one HTML file with a `<canvas>` and a `<script type="module">`. Use only the calls below; there are no `Mesh`, `Material`, `Object3D` or `WebGLRenderer` classes.

## Rules

- `await Engine.create({ canvas })` before anything else; `engine.scene` is the world.
- `await scene.load(url)` returns the model's root entity; `entity.bounds.center` and `.size` frame it.
- Units: meters; degrees for `transform.rotation`, `rotateX/Y/Z`, `OrbitControls`; lux for `scene.sun.intensity` (100000 = clear noon); hours for `scene.sky.timeOfDay`; seconds for `dt`.
- Axes: left-handed, +X right, +Y up, +Z forward; cameras and lights look along their entity's +Z.
- Components: `entity.set(Light, { type: 'Point', intensity: 800 })` adds or updates; `entity.get(Light)` returns a live view or `undefined`; `entity.add`, `entity.remove`, `entity.has`. Field names are camelCase (`intensity`, `fovY`, `timeOfDayHours`); enum fields take the enumerator name as a string; entity fields take an `Entity` or null; asset fields take `{ guid }`.
- Animate in `engine.onFrame(dt => { ... })`, then call `engine.run()`. `OrbitControls` updates itself every frame.
- Assets from another origin need CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin) under either build.

## Example

```js
import { Engine, OrbitControls, Light } from '@openengine/web';
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas');
if (!canvas) throw new Error('The page needs a <canvas> element.');
const engine = await Engine.create({ canvas });
const robot = await engine.scene.load('models/robot.glb');
const controls = new OrbitControls(engine.scene.camera, canvas);
controls.target.copy(robot.bounds.center);
engine.scene.sky.timeOfDay = 9.5;
engine.scene.create('lamp').set(Light, { type: 'Point', intensity: 800 });
engine.onFrame(dt => robot.transform.rotateY(20 * dt));
engine.run();
```

## Reference

- [README](README.md): the ten calls, adding components, threads and hosting.
- [opengine.d.ts](ts/opengine.d.ts): Engine, Scene, Entity, TransformView, OrbitControls, SunView, SkyView, OpenEngineError.
- [components.d.ts](ts/components.d.ts): the reflected components and their fields, with units (the first six today; the generated file names every component).
